chapter: Cab Calloway, Lunceford, Hampton and Armstrong, 1941-45
title: Earl Carruthers and Harry Carney on baritone
summary: McRae praises both baritone players and calls Carney a once-in-a-lifetime player and Duke's work lasting art.

Like in Louie -- (inaudible) with Louie, there will never be another Louie Armstrong, or a Duke Ellington. The type of things that Duke would do to give to the world.

That you can go into their works and pull out some of the chords and some of things that we're trying to do -- some of the things we're doing now. It's still in their works.
